### Summary

When snapy is built, CMake writes one header, `configure.h`, that records which optional pieces went into the
library: the communication backend, CUDA support and the two NetCDF output paths. A run can only choose among what
was compiled. This section lists those definitions and what reads each of them.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Records the compiled alternatives in `configure.h`.

**Data.** Build options in; macros and path constants out.

**Placement.** `configure_file`, before compilation.

**Activation.** Always generated; feature macros follow the build options.

**Guarantee / limits.** A run can select only compiled alternatives; no fallback is implied.

**Evidence.** Tests below, @tbl-ch12-macros-tests; solver ctests were not run.
:::

| definition | producer | reader or role |
|---|---|---|
| `USE_C10D_GLOO` | always defined | no reader in the sources; not a backend choice |
| `USE_UCX` or `NOT_USE_UCX` | the `UCX` option | process-group implementation and the platform default backend |
| `USE_CUDA` or `NOT_USE_CUDA` | the `CUDA` option | device dispatch and test availability |
| `NETCDFOUTPUT` or `NO_NETCDFOUTPUT` | the `NETCDF` option | output implementation |
| `PNETCDFOUTPUT` or `NO_PNETCDFOUTPUT` | the `PNETCDF` option | parallel output implementation |
| `NMASS` | the cache value | legacy index layout; must stay zero |
| `DISPATCH_MACRO` | nvcc detection | `__host__ __device__` under nvcc, empty otherwise |
| `KINTERA_ROOT_DIR`, `HARP_ROOT_DIR` | the configure directories | path constants; no reader in the sources |
| `_GLIBCXX_USE_CXX11_ABI` | the Torch probe | every compiled translation unit |
| `HAVE_AVX512_CPU_DEFINITION`, `HAVE_AVX2_CPU_DEFINITION` | the compiler setup | Torch headers |
| `COMMUX_WITH_CUDA_RUNTIME` | `CUDA` together with UCX | the commux CUDA sidecar |

: Generated definitions at the pin. {#tbl-ch12-macros-definitions}

### Derivation

No physical derivation applies. Macro substitution happens before compilation, so a run-time selection is
restricted to the compiled alternatives, and the complement macros document an excluded feature rather than
implementing a fallback. Check line `[C7]` enumerates that containment over four compiled sets and three
alternatives: a value is selectable at run time exactly when it was compiled, the selectable set never exceeds
the compiled one, and it never meets the complement [check `src/snapy_report/ch12/checks/configuration_check.py`,
output `src/snapy_report/ch12/checks/configuration_check.out`].

### Numerical method

Generation uses `configure_file` on {{< code configure.h.in >}}; readers then compile the available path. The
ABI and backend selection must agree across the linked libraries. These definitions have no cell location,
ghost stencil or RK-stage dependence. The one run-time consumer this chapter follows is `default_backend`
({{< code src/layout/layout.cpp default_backend >}}), which returns `ucx` under `USE_UCX` except on Darwin and
`gloo` otherwise.

```{python}

#| fig-cap: "Generated macros and compile definitions: labelled boxes show inputs and decisions in evaluation order. This is a configuration or stencil diagram, not measured data."
#| fig-alt: "option/cache; configure.h; compiled reader; runtime options."
```

### Code

**How to use it.** Select features through CMake, then regenerate and rebuild; do not define these names in YAML.
For example, `cmake -S . -B build -DCUDA=OFF -DUCX=OFF` selects the CPU and non-UCX alternatives. `-DUCX=OFF` overrides the non-Apple default; macOS already defaults to OFF.
Inspect the generated `configure.h` before attributing an unavailable backend to runtime input.
A runtime selection cannot supply a library excluded at compilation; the template itself performs no input validation.

{{< code configure.h.in >}} contains this selection step:

```cpp
// UCX
#define @UCX_OPTION@

// CUDA
#define @CUDA_OPTION@
```

CMake substitutes each `@...@` token with its positive or complement macro. This is the compiled-set boundary
in `[C7]`, not a runtime fallback; `default_backend` reads `USE_UCX` as described above.

| what | code link | symbol | switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| template | {{< code configure.h.in >}} | `DISPATCH_MACRO` | `configure.h` |
| params | {{< code cmake/parameters.cmake >}} | `NMASS` | `configure.h` |
| compiler | {{< code cmake/compilers.cmake >}} | `HAVE_AVX2_CPU_DEFINITION` | `configure.h` |
| abi | {{< code CMakeLists.txt >}} | `_GLIBCXX_USE_CXX11_ABI` | `configure.h` |
| sidecar | {{< code src/CMakeLists.txt >}} | `COMMUX_WITH_CUDA_RUNTIME` | `CUDA` |
| backend default | {{< code src/layout/layout.cpp default_backend >}} | `default_backend` | `USE_UCX` |

: Implementation sites for the generated macros. {#tbl-ch12-macros-code}

1. Map each option to its macro name in {{< code cmake/parameters.cmake >}}; the anchor `NMASS` is set there
   when empty.
2. Substitute the names into {{< code configure.h.in >}}; the anchor `DISPATCH_MACRO` is defined there under
   nvcc.
3. Compile the readers; the anchor `default_backend` in {{< code src/layout/layout.cpp default_backend >}}
   is the one that selects the communication backend from `USE_UCX`.

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_process_group.<b>` | with `BACKEND` unset the backend is the platform's compiled default | exact string equality | the test's expected default helper |
| `configuration_check.py` `[C7]` (report check) | the compiled-alternative containment | exact symbolic or Boolean equality | the independent check |

: Source assertions, not new solver measurements. {#tbl-ch12-macros-tests}

The assertion is `EXPECT_EQ` in
{{< code tests/test_process_group.cpp LayoutOptions.DefaultsToPlatformCommunicationBackend >}}, against
`expected_default_backend` ({{< code tests/test_process_group.cpp expected_default_backend >}}).

No snapy runtime test is executed for this chapter. CUDA and multi-rank entries describe registration only.
The independent checks and their outputs are catalogued in @sec-ch15-ch12-tests.

The independent report check verifies the compiled-alternative containment in `[C7]`.[^ch12-macros-run]
It models the stated contract; it does not execute the compiled solver.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
The backend default test is the only indirect test of the preprocessor layer; there is no exhaustive macro
coverage. The definitions without a reader are retained as code facts, not as a public run-time API[^rg-acfcf8f38b7f].

The complete switch inventory is @sec-ch12-matrix.
:::
